newsitem.title: UK: Gas oil gets Asian boost, other Med products quiet.
newsitem.headline: Gas oil gets Asian boost, other Med products quiet.

text.p: Mediterranean oil products markets were dull on Tuesday apart from gas oil which was again supported by demand from Asia.
Naphtha held stable in quiet trade. Traders said Far East demand was slacker and petrochems were relaxed as cheaper alternative feedstocks such as propane met their needs.
"Propane is quite a good alternative to naphtha at the moment although the gap is closing," a trader said.
Discussion was thin and mainly quotes related but some traders assessed outright prices at around $178/$182 a tonne cif, though they said the emphasis was towards the softer side.
Gasoline held steady with supplies, particularly of low octane, remaining fairly tight, but balanced by slack spot demand. Prompt cargoes were valued around $207/$208 a tonne cif.

Asia continues to support the gas oil market with 0.2 percent able to attract around cif fob quotes +$3-4. Premiums could ease towards the month's end as the market prepares for the return of ISAB's Sicilian refinery.
Concern also exists about the prospect of the Asian arb closing.
"Local (Med) demand is not very great and prices will probably weaken," said one trader.
So far there are no concrete signs of the shutting of the arb, which has drawn nearly two million tonnes of European fuel eastwards.
Diesel was understood to be attracting only modest interest around high fob EN590 quotes +$2-3.
Fuel oil markets were again sleepy, with market talk of a large high sulphur shipment eastward but nothing confirmed. Prices were set to weaken, traders said, with demand softening.
A low sulphur straight-run cargo from Libya was offered, as were high sulphur Black Sea straight-runs from Tuapse.
Low sulphur cracked was again barely discussed.
